comment: CBI65 derives CBI64's availability baseline from what CBI48 committed. A vector states one journal's committed observations as code-and-cycle-index pairs and pins the derivation. Instants are the cycle instants a cadence on the shared schedule would have prepared, so a vector never names a time the journal could not hold.

schedule.comment: The instant of cycle N is start plus N intervals, which is what CBI48 records as a committed observation's instant.

vectors.name: the-most-recent-establishing-cycle-supplies-it
vectors.comment: Two current cycles: the later one wins, so a derivation that took the first would report a deadline five minutes early.

vectors.name: an-outage-does-not-move-it
vectors.comment: CBI64's C2 rule reconstructed from the record. Three offline cycles follow one current cycle and the baseline stays at the current one, so the deadline a resumed cadence computes is the one the interrupted cadence held.

vectors.name: a-withdrawal-establishes-current-policy
vectors.comment: A sweep that withdrew members still had a current poll before it ran, so its cycle moves the baseline exactly as a plain current one does.

vectors.name: recovery-after-an-outage-moves-it
vectors.comment: The endpoint returned mid-run. A derivation that stopped at the first outage would anchor the deadline before a recovery the record plainly shows.

vectors.name: a-run-that-never-reached-the-endpoint-has-none
vectors.comment: Every committed cycle is an outage, so nothing in the record says the host ever saw current policy. CBI49's answer to a missing baseline is unchanged: the first outage after resumption stops service.

vectors.name: an-empty-record-has-none
vectors.comment: A journal established and interrupted on its first attempt has committed nothing at all.

vectors.name: an-unclassifiable-observation-is-refused
vectors.comment: A stopped cycle is produced both for a poll that was not current and for a current poll whose sweep failed, so the record does not say whether it established anything. CBI48 cannot place one in front of a later cycle — it terminates the run in the same write — but the derivation reads a snapshot, so this is a reachable input rather than a manufactured path.

vectors.name: a-refusal-outranks-an-establishing-cycle-behind-it
vectors.comment: The refusal is not a fallback to whatever was derivable before it. A baseline computed from the cycles ahead of the unclassifiable one would be confidently wrong about everything after it.

classification.comment: The vocabulary's answer for every code it holds, so both roots agree on the classification and not only on the vectors that happen to exercise it. A null means the vocabulary does not answer, which a consumer must refuse rather than resolve.
